Long documents often contain repeated headers and footers. These elements are visually helpful to readers but can become noise in machine-readable output. A robust system should identify recurring page furniture without removing legitimate content that happens to repeat across sections. This instance belongs to page 1, paragraph 5, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

The most useful output format depends on the application. Markdown is convenient for human inspection and language models, while JSON is better for preserving block types, coordinates, page indices, and confidence values. Many production pipelines retain both representations. This instance belongs to page 1, paragraph 6, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

Text quality should be tested with normal paragraphs, headings, numbered sections, quotations, and deliberately varied sentence lengths. The goal is not to make the document visually complex, but to expose segmentation and ordering behavior in a controlled setting. This instance belongs to page 1, paragraph 7, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

A ten-page sample provides enough repetition to test pagination, batching, and page references without creating a large file. Because the document contains only embedded text, it should remain small and should not require optical character recognition. : Text Extraction Control

This page intentionally contains only selectable text.

Plain-text documents are useful as a control case because they isolate textual extraction from visua interpretation. When a file contains no photographs, diagrams, equations, or tables, differences between parsers are usually caused by line segmentation, multi-column ordering, headers, footers, and font encoding. This instance belongs to page 2, paragraph 1, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

Evaluation should distinguish exact character recovery from semantic usability. A system may reproduce every glyph but join unrelated columns, or it may normalize spacing and punctuation while preserving the intended meaning. Both behaviors matter in downstream retrieval and question answering applications. This instance belongs to page 2, paragraph 2, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

Page-level provenance is especially important in research workflows. A generated summary should be traceable to the source page, and extracted claims should retain enough location information for verification. This is easier when the parser emits structured blocks rather than one uninterrupted string. This instance belongs to page 2, paragraph 3, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.

A robust system should identify recurring page furniture without removing legitimate content that happens to repeat across sections. This instance belongs to page 2, paragraph 4, and is included to verify stable pagination and deterministic reading order.
